_rule: The agreement rule of specification section 11.1.12: two finite results agree when |a-b| <= 1e-12 * the line's scale, the scale taken per policy over the node's own values and the values of every node it reads. **Two measurements are recorded here, and they are not one number.** `ratios` are the worst this engine's vector run observed per identifier -- one operation over a handful of policies, where nothing stands in front of the operation to cancel. `models` are the worst any line of a whole shipped model observed, each at the size that model is run at here -- levels 4 and 5 over a thousand policies and eighty-three periods, where a chain of operations lets a rounding at magnitude one land on a difference of two near-equal quantities and come out two orders up in ratio terms; the two rollforward patterns over two policies and their own schedules, where the chain is the machine's. An identifier can read nought in `ratios` and still be the operation behind the worst line in `models`. A landing that worsens either moves the number here with the reason beside it, and nothing else may move it.
_measured: Measured with jax 0.4.38 / jaxlib 0.4.38 on darwin x86_64, core 0.9.0 (the development build of 1.0.0, before its version moved). Vector tolerances are acceptance budgets, never evidence of reference uncertainty. Every finite numeric reference is measured except the two explicitly reviewed expected arrays listed below, whose dtype and values must match their SHA-256. These arrays are rounded to six decimals and the agreement rule is not measurable from their published data; ordinary vector-budget checks still run. The live full-precision fund and ratchet tutorial references remain evidence under the agreement rule for those machines. excel.irr is restored: its 1e-7 tolerance does not make the exact zero-root reference imprecise. Updated 2026-09-23 from the first Linux run, jax 0.11.2 / jaxlib 0.11.2 on linux x86_64 (GitHub Actions): the engine's lock resolves the 0.4.38 floor only for darwin x86_64, so Linux runs current jax, and XLA's CPU code there moves three records inside the agreement rule's band. Each recorded number is now the larger of the two platforms'; the darwin run still reads at or below it. Updated 2026-10-22: `is_in` and `join` are measured for the first time, by the selection vectors (a filter's compound predicate, a semi and an anti join applied before the answer); both are exact.

_reasons.log10: 1.1e-17 of the line's scale, five orders inside the agreement rule's 1e-12. XLA's log10 is its own and 11.1.12 gives the transcendental family a relative tolerance rather than a bitwise contract.
_reasons.excel.yearfrac: 2.2e-16 of the line's scale, one place of a double. 11.1.34's denominators are 360, 365 and 366 and the day counts divided by them are exact; what parts the two engines is the order the 30/360 numerator's three terms are added in, which no clause fixes.
_reasons.projection.cumulative_survival: 1.5e-16, one place. A running product of one minus the decrement is a chain of multiplications and the two engines associate the chain the same way; what differs is the last rounding of each factor.
_reasons.projection.prospective_value: 1.5e-16, one place. 11.1.21's suffix sums divide by a product of discount factors, and a division by a product is not bitwise a product of divisions.
_reasons.finance.discount_factor: 5.6e-17, a quarter of a place. 11.1.30 allows relative error 1e-12 on the spot factors outright; a power taken as exp(log) on one engine and as a library pow on the other differs in the last bit.
_reasons.finance.compound: 4.6e-18. The same power, at the smaller magnitudes 11.1.29's own growth factors take.
_reasons.curve.spot_rate: 3.5e-18. Not an engine difference: both engines answer the line as the producer writes it, y0 + (y1 - y0) * (t - x0) / (x1 - x0), each operation rounded, and agree to the bit (a 1.0 change moved this engine off jnp.interp, which grouped the line the other way and fused its product and sum). The published expected array is the exact rate -- 0.04 at t = 2 between 0.02 and 0.06 -- and the rounded line answers 0.039999999999999994, a quarter of a place from it.
_reasons.finance.to_monthly: 1.4e-17 of the line's scale, a tenth of a place, and nought before the region pass was compiled. 11.1.29's twelfth root is exp(log(1+i)/12) and the compiler fuses the divide into the exponent, which is one rounding where the unfused form has two.
_reasons.excel.irr: 1.7e-18 of the line's scale, on window-irr (vectors/windows.json): the rate solved for [-100, 100] is the exact root nought, and this engine's bisection over the clause's bracket lands 1.7e-16 from it on a scale of 100 -- ordinary root finding, six orders inside the agreement rule's 1e-12, where the six-hundred-period zero root measured 9.3e-20. Moved when the perturbation vectors, the first published cases with a two-period stream, joined the measurement; measured with jax 0.4.38 / jaxlib 0.4.38 on darwin x86_64, the Linux figure not yet taken. The vector acceptance budget of 1e-7 conveys no reference uncertainty.
_reasons.exp: 1.6e-16 of the line's scale on the first Linux run, jax 0.11.2 / jaxlib 0.11.2 on linux x86_64 (GitHub Actions); exact (0.0) on darwin at jax 0.4.38. XLA 0.11's CPU exp is its own vectorised polynomial, one ulp from Polars on a vector cell; 11.1.12 gives the transcendental family a relative tolerance, not a bitwise contract. Four orders inside the agreement rule's band.
_reasons.cbrt: 1.6e-17 of the line's scale on the first Linux run, jax 0.11.2 / jaxlib 0.11.2 on linux x86_64 (GitHub Actions); exact (0.0) on darwin at jax 0.4.38. XLA 0.11 computes cbrt through its own routine rather than libm's, one ulp apart on one vector cell. Five orders inside the agreement rule's band.
_reasons.norm_cdf: 2.8e-17 of the line's scale, darwin x86_64 at jax 0.4.38, against the double nearest Phi worked to 60 digits: XLA's ndtr and a correctly rounded Phi part company in the last place on a few vector cells. 11.1.12 gives the transcendental family a relative tolerance rather than a bitwise contract, and every normal-range case also passes its own 1e-12 relative budget, the lower tail to -37.5 included. Five orders inside the agreement rule's band.
_reasons.excel.pv: 3.7e-16 of the line's scale, under two places of a double, since the kit's per-period cases joined the measurement: each period answers on this engine what the same operands answer per policy, to the bit, so the larger figure is new operand values, not a new path. 11.1.35 now takes (1+r)^-n as exp(-n log1p(r)) and 1-(1+r)^-n as -expm1(-n log1p(r)), so the 1e-12 holds however near nought the rate; exp, log1p and expm1 are the host's on the producer and XLA's here, and 11.1.12 holds the transcendental family to a relative band rather than the bit. Measured on darwin x86_64 at 3.7e-16; the first Linux x86_64 run (GitHub Actions, CPU) and the T4 both measure 9.6e-16, glibc's expm1 and log1p parting from darwin's in the last place, so the record holds the larger. Three orders inside the agreement rule's band.

level-4.reason: Every line bit-identical to Polars, darwin x86_64 at jax 0.4.38, since the engine rounds every product before the sum that reads it -- the arithmetic `*`, the recurrence, a rollforward's growth and charge, the present value and a curve's line between knots -- so the fused multiply-add that was this model's worst line (combined_decrement = 1 - (1 - q)(1 - w), 2.464166e-14 on darwin and 3.241326e-14 on the first Linux run, jax 0.11.2) is gone, and with it the one-place differences in the 32 lines that read it. No line has a ratio, so the node named is the first the comparison lists, as for the rollforward patterns. Linux not re-measured here: a maths call XLA 0.11 answers a place from Polars (exp, cbrt) would show on that run as a ratio inside the band, and moves this record with its reason.

fund.reason: the single-state fund of the rollforward tutorial: grow, charge and floor on one balance over twelve monthly periods, 2 policies, 10 value-bearing nodes, 5 of them numeric. exactly equal in value to Polars on every line, including the balances. A compiled rollforward is a serialized chain of multiplies, adds and maxima applied one period at a time, and 16.1 fixes the order: there is no reassociation for a compiler to take and no closed form standing beside the recurrence for the two engines to differ over. The compared set is every value-bearing node of the artifact -- the running balances through the exporter's own re-track on the Polars side and through the scan on this one -- and every line meets the fixed strict floor, 1e-10 plus 1e-12 of the reference value, as well as the agreement rule's band. The complete-frame test permits only the artifact-declared Int32 to Int64 and List(Int32) to List(Int64) normalization; every other physical dtype matches. This records exact declared values and floating results, not identical physical frame layouts.

ratchet.reason: the multi-state GMDB ratchet of the rollforward tutorial: a growth on the fund and a gated lift of the benefit base to the fund's within-period close over sixty monthly periods, 2 policies, 13 value-bearing nodes, 7 of them numeric. The node named here is the worst of a set that is entirely nought, so it is the first of the tie rather than the hardest line; the hardest line is gmdb@1, the cross-state read at @eop that is the whole reason the operation exists, and it is exactly equal in value too. exactly equal in value to Polars on every line, including the balances.
